html:
"Arabian pastoral nomads" is the map's label for the herding peoples of the Arabian desert and steppe between 1500 and 700 BCE, outside the oasis towns and the farming kingdoms of the south.

They moved with sheep, goats and, increasingly, camels between seasonal pastures and wells. The one humped camel, the dromedary, was domesticated in Arabia around the end of the second millennium BCE. It let people cross long dry stretches and carry heavy loads, which made possible the caravans of the incense trade from Saba in the south to the Mediterranean.

These nomads first appear by name in Assyrian records. In 853 BCE an Arab chief called Gindibu brought a thousand camels to fight the Assyrians at the Battle of Qarqar. They were the ancestors of the later Arabs and of the Bedouin.
sum: "Arabian pastoral nomads" is the map's label for the herding peoples of the Arabian desert and steppe between 1500 and 700 BCE, outside the oasis towns and the farming kingdoms of the south.
